the target. This file is a CLAIM about what exists, and the run inherits its gaps: a notional
zone with no port behind it produces a package the reviewer must block ('no bindable
interface'), and the round parks. Before you launch, walk each object you name below and
confirm a real thing answers to it on the device.

agents behaved correctly: they disclosed the impossibility rather than fabricating a binding
(VT-18). The defect was in this file.

_note: KEEP THIS BLOCK for any multi-pipeline program. It is the machine-readable counterpart to
requirements.md's 'Why this is sequenced' section, and the two must agree.
THE TEST that decides the value of `kind`:
Is every value the downstream domain needs knowable BEFORE the upstream domain runs?
yes -> 'parallel'   ... the values belong in the INTERFACE CONTRACT
no  -> 'sequenced'  ... the value must ride a DAG EDGE (inter-pipeline chaining)
Getting this wrong in the parallel direction is the expensive one: the downstream leg starts
with a value nobody could have known, and either guesses or stalls.
interdependency.chainedValue: {{the value that crosses the edge, or null if parallel}}
interdependency.direction_note: {{which leg produces, which consumes, and what the consumer must NOT do — e.g. 'the consumer re-states the chained value and is forbidden from recomputing it'}}
